newsitem.title: USA: Lawmakers urge House leaders not to sell off PMA's.
newsitem.headline: Lawmakers urge House leaders not to sell off PMA's.

text.p: A bipartisan group of House lawmakers are urging Republican leaders to reject any plans to sell off the U.S. power marketing administrations in a bid to balance the budget.

In a March 21 letter released Tuesday, 63 lawmakers said before making any proposals, House leaders should wait for the results of a General Accounting Office study on the impact of selling off the federal assets.
The House Budget Committee is reportedly considering proposing the sale of the power marketing administrations, which market power generated at federal dams, in its fiscal 1998 budget plan.
In their letter to the comittee's chairman Rep. John Kasich of Ohio and House Speaker Newt Gingrich, the lawmakers said it would be a bad idea.

"While we understand your desire to look for ways to balance the budget, we believe that any effort to sell these PMAs is unjustified at this time in light of the questionable budgetary benefits it will have," their letter said.
"Likewise, in our opinion,such a plan will also have a detrimental impact on the electric rates of consumers in our districts," it said.
The GAO report is due at the end of this month.
The Clinton administration two years ago proposed selling off the PMAs to help trim the budget gap, but dropped the idea when lawmakers balked at losing the cheap electricity in their areas.
